en:
We sure do! This one comes recommended. Get the best for
just 6,300 yen!
(6,300 yen. Take thirty percent off, and... I have to try for 4,410 yen. That's a pretty tall order.)
Open fire...
Yikes! What!? What's that she said?
Oh, uh, yeah, don't mind her.
6,300 yen? Can you go a little lower?

Ohh, I get it now, the lady there put ya up to this. Look,
friend, I wish I could, but we're hurtin', too.

But the customer is king, so I'll give ya a deal! Hmm...
6,000! How's 6,000 yen sound to ya?
Surely you can do better.

Keep pushin' like that, and you'll drive us to the
poorhouse, I swear. But all right, 5,800 yen! That eats up
our profit. How's that strike you!?
How about half price? 3,150 yen.

That's plain evil, my friend! We're not runnin' a charity
here.

Givin' up on our profit margin, let's see...  5,800 yen!
That's the best I can do. How 'bout it?

You know, this store... It's got a unique charm. Not like
those big appliance stores. It has a real sense of welcoming
to it.

That's just it. With a place like ours, it's important to be
a good neighbor, a good member of the local community.

It can't be easy for you, but it really speaks to your
shop's status around town.

Ah, now here's a man who understands! Ya know, I like you!
If I could, I'd just give it to you as a gift.

You're pretty likable yourself. Maybe a part of the shop's
charm comes from you, huh?

My friend, I dare say you got the best of me. I'll drop
right down to 5,000 yen.
(The target's 4,410 yen. Just a little more.)
That'll be 5,800 yen on the nose. Thank you kindly!
You got an electric toothbrush.

(It's nowhere near the 4,410 yen target. I'll have to make
up for it with my next purchase.)

This toothbrush⑬it isn't the latest model, is it? It's last
season's, if I'm not mistaken.

Precisely why I can't let ya have it for so low. The latest
models cost much, much more, ya know?

But wait too long, and won't it just go unsold? Are you sure
you don't want to go lower?

Well, now you're just being insulting. This might not be the
newest, but it's still good. If ya don't like that, you can
take your business elsewhere.
(Urk... This isn't looking good.)

You know, I bet the ladies consider you pretty handsome,
huh? You must knocking 'em dead left and right.

Huh? Well, uh, yeah. Hahaha, ya think so? Maybe when I was
younger...

"Ken-chan, I want a microwave. I want you to turn me on and
heat me up." That actually happened! And on more than one
occasion. Heheh.

Sheesh, friend, ya sure know how to make a guy happy,
bringin' up sweet memories like that. Tell ya what, I'll let
it go for 4,500.
(Whoa. He really went down.)
Sold! I'll take it, then.
That'll be 4,500 yen on the nose. Thank you kindly!

(The target was 4,410 yen, so I'd say that went okay. Next
up, a leopard-print skirt.)
That'll be 5,000 yen on the nose. Thank you kindly!

(The target was 4,410 yen, so I fell a little short. I'll
need to make up the difference with the leopard-print skirt.)

(Urk... This isn't looking good. I can't push him any
further.)
You certainly are generous. I'm impressed.

Ah, you say that, but we still don't have a deal, do we?
You're a sly one, friend.

I'm almost there. I just need one last nudge. Though I do
feel kind of bad for taking advantage of your generosity.
Okay then, 4,500 yen! How's that grab ya?

Kind of a half-assed figure, don't you think? What do you
say we cut the loose change right out?
Nnngh... All right, buddy, I surrender! 4,000 yen it is!
Deal!
That'll be 4,000 yen on the nose. Thank you kindly!

(Yes! The target was 4,410 yen, so I got well over a thirty percent
discount. Looking good. Next up, the leopard-print skirt.)

Can you go down to 5,000 yen? It'd really help me out if you
could.
Sorry, no can do. I'll settle for 5,600 yen, though.

My friend, this is the best I can do. 5,500 yen! I ain't
budgin' any further.
That'll be 5,500 yen on the nose. Thank you kindly!

(Hmm... I fell way short of the 4,410 yen target. I'll have
to make up for it with the leopard-print skirt.)
Ya think so? Thanks.

(No good. The guy's turned cold. I can't push him any
further.)

All right. The first rule in haggling: praise your foe.
Successful negotiation means winnin' the hearts and minds of
your opponent.

And don't praise the merchandise. It's the same as with
women⑬don't let 'em know you're interested.
Right. Makes sense.

Rule number two: never name your price. Let your opponent
reveal their hand first.

Hmm. That rule applies to a lot more than just haggling.
I've got to hand it to you Osaka ladies⑬you're pretty tough
customers, no pun intended.

The third and final rule: respect the merchandise. Merchants
usually take great pride in their wares, after all.

Sayin' something's old or scuffed to knock down the price...
That's a big no-no.

Hagglin' in a way that hurts the merchant's pride is an ugly
thing.

A fight in which both sides respect each other's worth and
end it with a handshake⑬that's the perfect way to haggle. You'd do well to remember that.

And there you have it, the three rules of Osaka-style
hagglin'. You get all that, rookie?
Yeah. Loud and clear.

Right then, go get the items I've requested. And remember,
10,000 yen or less!

Before ya go off to battle, ya wanna hear my rules for
hagglin' again?
Please. I'd love to hear them again.
All right, get the wax outta your ears and listen good!
I'm good. Got it all down.
Good, that's the spirit. Remember, if ya don't get thirty percent off each thing, you'll be over budget. Now get out there and show 'em what you can do!
Shoppin' in Sotenbori is a battle against the shop.
If ya got the time, I can show you the ropes. How about it?
Sounds interesting. Yes, please.
Good! No one better to learn ya how!

Okay, here's what you do. Here's 10,000 yen. I want you to
take this and do a little shoppin' for me.

I need an electric toothbrush, a leopard-print skirt, and a
pair of red high heels.
Huh? I'm doing your shopping?

Right. But only after I teach ya the fine art of hagglin' in
Sotenbori. We'll start with the basics!
I appreciate the offer, but I'll have to pass.
Oh come on now, that's cold of ya.
So, uh, you saved me?

You're about as sharp as a bag of wet mice. I couldn't bear
to watch. You don't know the first thing about shoppin' in Sotenbori, do ya?
It's different from shopping anywhere else?

If I didn't step in and take ya under my wing, you woulda
bought at that shop's askin' price. That's just plain wrong.

Shoppin' in Sotenbori is a battle against the shop! Everyone
here haggles. In fact, you'd be crazy not to.
Really? A battle, huh?

That's right. Tell ya what, this old gal's gonna be your
guardian angel and teach ya how to shop in Sotenbori. How about it?
Saejima-san, please deliver my husband's letter to our son Masao in Tsukimino.
Our son told us he's working at a place called Apocalypse.
Oh, Saejima-san. Could I trouble you for something?
Hm? Oh, you're the mother of that runaway kid, aren't ya?
Yes, my son Masao. Um... you're traveling to Tsukimino, right?
That's where Masao is. I'm not sure how to ask this, but... Would you deliver this letter to him?
You got a <Color:8>Letter to Masao<Color:Default>.
I can, but wouldn't it get there quicker if ya just mailed it?
I don't want to do that because Masao lives in the company dorm, and he doesn't want his coworkers to know he's getting mail from home.
The hell's up with that? He embarrassed?
Saejima-san, I know it's a bother, but please? It's a letter from his father.
Sounds serious. Is he disowning the boy or somethin'?
I don't know what it says. Ever since our son left, my husband has barely said a word.
Alright. I'll help ya out. Where can I find yer boy?
He's working at a restaurant called Apocalypse in Tsukimino.
Okay. Apocalypse.
That's right. I don't like asking you to do this, but... I would be very grateful.
Hm? Do you want something?
Ya leavin' the village?
Well, yes. I'm leaving for Tsukimino. I don't want to be stuck here forever.
That so? Ya know, it's bad for the village to be losin' so many young people.
I know that. But I'm so sick of this place. I can't stand how boring it is.
Masao...
You're Saejima-san, aren't you? Aren't you from some big city yourself? Which one?
What's the use of knowin' that?
Because, like, you get why I want to leave, right? You know how cool the big city is.
My dad wouldn't listen to anything I said about it. Every time I brought it up, he'd just smack me and say becoming a hunter was my only choice.
That's why I'm running away.
Runnin' away?
My husband doesn't know that Masao is leaving. He would never allow it.
Ya realize yer pa's gonna blow his stack when he finds out.
What, are you trying to stop me?
Nah. This ain't the sort of thing for strangers to meddle in.
Agreed. Well, it's now or never. I need to be gone before dad gets back.
*sob* Remember you can always come home.
It'll be okay, Mom. I'm eighteen now. Have a little faith in me.
My son...

en: (Hope the kid does all right for himself.)
You work here at Apocalypse, right? This a host club?
Yes. Are you coming in?
(Some restaurant, Masao.)
I heard there's a guy who works here named Masao. He around?
Masao? What's he to you?
Just an acquaintance. Is he here or not?
Tch. He took off after only one day. Shirked a 300,000 yen payment.
A client he was handling left an unpaid bill. It's up to the host to cover it when that sort of thing happens.
But instead of being responsible, he just vanished. We've been looking for him everywhere.
We'll track that idiot down eventually and settle it!
Bullshit. You set him up, didn't ya? Took advantage of the fact he didn't know up from down in this city.
What kinda outfit pairs up a shady client with the new guy?
Anyway, I guess that means I won't find him here. See ya.
Tch. The nerve of some people.
(So where the hell did Masao get to?)
What the hell? This guy's like a machine...
Ya had enough? Already?
Jackass!
Yes, that's enough.
Our boys make their living with their looks. Please don't damage the merchandise anymore.
The owner of Apocalypse. Would you accept my apology on their behalf and we can all move on?
What about Masao's debt?
It's fine. It's all been settled.
Huh? What do you mean?
Masao's parents repaid the debt in full. 500,000 yen. They paid without hesitation when I explained the situation to them by phone.
The debt was 300,000 yen. How'd it get to half a million?
The extra 200,000 was offered by the father. He said it was to compensate us for Masao running away from the club. A most reasonable man.
We have no need for further communication with you, Masao. You should be thankful that your parents settled your debt. Farewell.
500,000 yen... That's gotta be a lot of money for yer folks.
Still don't wanna read the letter from yer pa?
Uh... May I see it, now? Please?
Yeah. 'Course.
Dear Masao⑬ In the time since you left, I've realized something. This day had to come.
Our village, so isolated from the rest of society, must have been deadly dull in your eyes. It was only natural that you would want to leave for the city.
I tried to tie you down. I did not want to let you out of my sight, even though you're old enough to be on your own.
It was for my own ego that I did that. And I knew it was hurting you...
But, I have no education. I've never lived in a town, let alone a city. Can you imagine how worried I was about my only child walking into a world I know nothing about?
When you defied me, I was furious. That was how I felt then, and it's how I feel now.
But, at the same time, I also find myself feeling proud. Because you are my son.
You stepped out into the big, wide world. That shows courage. Your mother and I will comfort ourselves with this thought. Don't worry about us. You are free to spread your wings.
I'm sure you will face many hurdles, but I know you can overcome anything. Never give up, Masao.
Don't let the city folk intimidate you. You're my son. I could not be more proud to be your father.
So don't give up, Masao. Never, ever, ever give up.
"I look forward to the day we meet again. However long I have to wait, I'll keep waiting."
"On that day, you'll come to me as a man in his own right. And that's when I'll say to you..."
"I'm sorry I could only raise you in a tiny village like this. I'm sorry for keeping you cooped up. I'm sorry for not listening..."
